newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA PM SEES LOWER MTH INFLATION BY END-97.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA PM SEES LOWER MTH INFLATION BY END-97.

text.p: Romania's monthly inflation should be between one and two percent until year end, down from previous forecasts of two to three percent, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said on Thursday.

"According to preliminary data, inflation is estimated at about one or little over one percent in July," Ciorbea told a news conference. "By the end of the year, it will be between one to two percent against an initial forecast of two to three percent."
Monthly inflation fell to 2.3 percent in June from a record 30.7 percent in March after the centrist coalition government had liberalised prices of fuel, energy and staples.

Earlier on Thursday, the International Monetary Fund chief negotiator for Romania told Reuters the annual year-on-year inflation for 1997 was expected to be 130 percent or somewhat less, higher than earlier estimates of 90 percent.

Poul Thomsen, who ended a month-long assessment of Romania's reform progress, said the upward revision in the year-on-year inflation followed stronger than expected inflation figures earlier in the year.
Thomsen said he was confident monthly inflation would be about two percent by the end of 1997.
Ciorbea gave no year-on-year estimate for the year-end. Consumer prices were 101.2 percent up in June from last December, according to latest data.
